# Shared portfolio consumer recordings (B0–B3b)

B3b adds `asset_summary_cases.json`, canonical B-owned AssetSummary recordings for F01/F11/F18/F10. Scope/snapshot IDs and values match the corresponding A snapshot fixtures; incomplete F10 retains null positions/total. JSON Schema: `docs/wealth/asset_summary_v1.schema.json`; bank reader and integration handoff: `docs/wealth/manual_flow_b3b.md`. These recordings are development-only and never sent to bank transaction endpoints.

Contract: local 00 v0.3 (latest contents supplied on 2026-10-08), sections 6.2/6.4/7. The initial F01 is a complete snapshot/plan envelope for B's read-only development preview. It is a seed for A/B to align, not a declaration that A's production schema has been implemented or agreed through code review. A owns the production portfolio schema, provider and allocation/sliders; B has not created competing production types.

`assessment=null` is deliberate: the example must not create a formal assessment or authorize a customer. Ratios are the contract's F01 example, not an algorithm or production recommendation. No candidates or trade commands are invented. All IDs refer to imaginary fixture objects. The preview never sends these IDs to a bank endpoint.

`f18.json` and `f10.json` are explicit read-only asset-display samples (two accounts/held cash and missing valuation). The asset samples never read or write a customer database. F13 is checked against the existing simulated bank in `tests/integration/test_wealth_portfolio_consumer_baseline.py`, with isolated databases and both the bank-layer authorization fixture and the real HTTP confirm/TOTP chain.

`provider.py` is a test-only replay provider with `snapshot(case)`, `plan(case)`, `recommend(case)` and `revise(selection, case=...)`. It is not installed in the production router. F01 recommendations are deliberately empty; only its recorded no-op selection can be replayed. Unknown revisions or a plan for an unrecorded snapshot raise an error instead of inventing A's algorithm. Extend the recordings with A before implementing B1/B2 consumers.

F09 now records initial cash/stable/growth groups, three-family stable/growth batches, A/C and C-only/paused-A cases, null share classification, incomplete history, risk mismatch, and unavailable metadata. `next_groups` is a recorded second batch. These candidates are synthetic UI fixtures, never imported into the bank catalog. The development-only TypeScript provider in `FixtureProductProvider.ts` replays the recording and optional details/comparison. It is separate from the B0 Python replay provider and does not implement A's suitability/ranking algorithm.

B's candidate consumer types are type-only aliases to this shared recording's shape in `services/wealth.ts`, including nullable metadata and the cross-bucket risk case. No second production portfolio schema is created. Once A's canonical types are available, import them in the consumer boundary and validate its actual output. The recording is not proof that A's provider is implemented.

F11 records seven selected families and one exact revision (S1 15%, S2 5%, other weights unchanged). The DEV consumer only replays those outputs; other revisions fail explicitly. Sample prepare has no bank execution ID and never sends synthetic product IDs to the bank. The separate B2 integration tests use actual simulated-bank products and isolated databases to verify grouped confirmation, MFA, holds, cancellation, old-position differences and settlement dependencies. See `docs/wealth/manual_flow_b2.md` for the server-owned A adapter and its integration boundary.

These recordings do not certify B3–B6/J01–J23 or all F02–F24 cases. Extend the shared fixture directory with A as each contract is implemented; never silently change field meanings. Integration must validate actual provider output as well as sample files.

F23 records 12 orders and 10 lots aggregated into 9 position rows, separate accounts/product versions, full locking, cancellation eligibility and explicit published quote observations. `FixtureTableProvider.ts` only replays those facts; matching v1 detail observations have the same date/NAV as the tables and unrecorded v2 details fail explicitly. Browser interaction never submits fixture IDs to bank APIs. F23's independent paging/selection/detail portion is implemented; actual cash-flow returns and four time grains remain B3d. See `docs/wealth/manual_flow_b3a.md` and the isolated bank HTTP tests in `tests/integration/test_wealth_tables.py`. The live bank table entry is separate and uses the authenticated user's existing database.

Development URL: `http://127.0.0.1:3000/?wealth-dev=1` (log in with the existing demo account). Vite development only; the production build excludes the viewer. The new portfolio prepare API returns `PORTFOLIO_PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` until A's server adapter is registered; there is no production fixture bypass. The separate **手选模拟产品** entry uses the currently authenticated account and existing catalog/assessment/preview/confirm/verify/execute APIs; it does not send fixture IDs to the bank. It can change simulated funds only after the user's existing personal confirmation and MFA. The browser check stops at preview; full submission/cancellation is tested only in the isolated database. Open HUMAN-controlled tasks on the selected account block the manual preview entry; continuation stays in the original task UI.
